newsitem.title: USA: Sex allegations cloud sportscaster Albert's future.
newsitem.headline: Sex allegations cloud sportscaster Albert's future.

text.p: Renowned sportscaster Marv Albert faced possible career meltdown Wednesday following his indictment for allegedly assaulting a woman who refused a sexual favour.

Albert, one of the most recognisable voices of sports in America, was scheduled to call Saturday's basketball playoff game in Miami between the Chicago Bulls and Miami Heat for NBC, but network executives met to discuss Albert's future without reaching a decision.
A spokesman for NBC Sports declined comment Wednesday on any of those meetings and was unable to say when a decision might be announced.

Albert, 53, was charged Monday in Arlington Circuit Court with one felony count of forcible sodomy and one misdemeanor count of assault and battery after the alleged incident in an Arlington, Virginia hotel room Feb. 12.
The sports commentator denied the charges and his agent called them "preposterous."

His colleagues and the world of sports were shocked by the allegations. "It's impossible for me to envision Marv Albert doing what he is accused of doing," wrote colleague Phil Mushnick in the New York Post.
Others feared the charges would jeopardise the Brooklyn-born Albert's highly successful career, during which he has become almost as well recognised as the sports stars he covers.

"Marv's business ventures are 100 percent dependent on his ability to perform," said Bob Williams, president of Burns Sports Celebrity Service. "Marv has worked years to craft a public image and right now that's tainted, regardless of guilt or innocence. What a shame."
The sportscaster denied the charges in strong terms when they were revealed Tuesday. His agent Evan Bell Wednesday called all the charges "preposterous" and said Albert was "very upset."

Police said Albert allegedly became enraged with the 41-year-old woman, threw her on the bed, bit her violently on the back 15 times and forced her to perform oral sex. New York newspapers, which splashed the story on front pages Wednesday, quoted police sources as saying the woman had refused Albert's request to join him for sex with another man.
WRC-TV in Washington reported Wednesday that Albert's accuser herself faced a criminal charge for allegedly threatening to kill her former boyfriend.

The woman has pleaded not guilty to the misdemeanor charge, according to the local television report, which quoted court documents. The alleged threats were made in three cellular telephone calls placed to the boyfriend March 13.

Apart from NBC, Albert also broadcasts for Madison Square Garden Network in New York, where he is famous as the decades-long commentator for the New York Knicks of the National Basketball Association and the New York Rangers of the National Hockey League.
Albert, who is divorced and has four adult children, was expected to appear for arraignment in Arlington court at a time to be agreed with his lawyer and officials there.
Forcible sodomy carries a penalty of five years to life in prison and assault and battery is punishable by up to 12 months and a $2,500 fine.
